# SLP Self Learning Platform

> SLP, the Self Learning Platform: an agent-powered hub for self-learners.

## Introduction

- [Overview](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/overview.md): SLP is a self-hosted study environment you fully own: it runs on your machine, needs no subscription, and works with any agent and any model, local or paid.
- [Getting started](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/getting-started.md): Three things, then one prompt.
- [Installation](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/install.md): [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) manages Python and the dependencies. Install it once, then clone.
- [Setup](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/setup.md): Open your agent at the repo root and send the prompt. It detects which agent it is and exposes the skills in that agent's format: symlinks if it supports them, conversion if not.
- [Init your first topic](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/init.md): A topic is anything you study: a book, a certification, a paper, a course. Run `/slp-init` and the agent interviews you, creates the folder, checks your level and offers a dedicated teacher.
- [Run the app](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/cli.md): Starts the local server and opens the notebook in your browser. If a server is already running, it just opens the page.
- [Three windows](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/windows.md): Side by side. Two monitors help.
- [Language](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/language.md): Each topic sets default languages for what the agent writes. Ask for another in any single request ("give me the exam in English") without touching the file. The agent chats in whatever language you write in.
- [Dictation](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/dictation.md): Dictate notes or answer oral exam questions out loud. Runs locally with Whisper; without it, the mic falls back to your OS dictation.
- [Profiles](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/profiles.md): How the agent layer and dictation run. Chosen at setup, changeable in `/settings`. The core is the same in all of them.

## Skills

- [Session](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/slp-session.md): Entry point of a study session. Surveys every topic, asks what you want to do today and hands off to the right skill. It orchestrates; it doesn't write.
- [Agent setup](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/slp-setup.md): Exposes `agent/skills` and `agent/agents` in the running agent's native format, without touching anything versioned.
- [New topic](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/slp-init.md): Registers a new topic so the first session starts with a clear mission and the level already measured.
- [Summarize](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/slp-summarize.md): Summarizes a text and appends it to a note, following the format the notes already use.
- [Teach](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/slp-teach.md): Teaches so it ends up understood, not memorized. Probes your real level, plans the topic as a dependency graph and builds it node by node from truths you already accept.
- [Exercises](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/slp-exercises.md): An exam tests whether something was understood. An exercise forces you to use it to produce something new: code, an ADR, a critique, an explanation.
- [Exam](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/slp-exam.md): Builds a JSON exam from content you paste, audited first against the topic's progress. You sit it in the app, which shuffles the questions.
- [Grade](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/slp-grade.md): Checks each rubric or prompt point, says what's missing (not just "it's wrong"), and records it so review and the next session can use it.
- [Review](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/slp-review.md): Spaced, interleaved review with Leitner cards. Mixes topics, prioritizes what failed, and rewrites questions so they require recall, not recognition.

## Agents

- [Researcher](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/researcher.md): Verifies a fact or maps a topic and returns a short report with sources. Used before teaching anything that isn't certain. Works in an isolated context.
- [Teacher](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/teacher.md): One per topic, generated by [slp-init](slp-init.md). A specialist who would teach this in real life, never a generic "\<area> teacher".

## Folders

- [Topic folder](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/topics.md): Everything about a topic lives in one folder, as Markdown and JSON. It reads fine on GitHub, in Obsidian or in any editor.
- [topic.json](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/topic-json.md): Identity and preferences of a topic. Written by [slp-init](slp-init.md), completed by [slp-session](slp-session.md).
- [learning.md](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/learning-md.md): The topic's memory: what you've shown you know, and what you got wrong and corrected. Every skill reads it before writing.
- [notes/](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/notes.md): Summaries, lessons and your own notes, numbered. The app's editor splits a file by `#`, and renders Mermaid and LaTeX.
- [exams/](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/exams.md): One folder per exam, named by unit (`ch-01`, `domain-02`). Attempts are named by the minute they were made and point at questions by position.
- [exercises/](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/exercises.md): Applied work. A `prompt.md` from [slp-exercises](slp-exercises.md) and your submissions in `attempts/`, any extension.
- [progress/](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/progress.md): Where you are and what happened. Written by the skill that produced the event, never by `slp-session`.
- [agent/](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/agent-dir.md): The single source of the agent layer. Skills use the Agent Skills format: `name` + `description` frontmatter, instructions below. Agents without skill support read the matching `SKILL.md` by hand, as `AGENTS.md` explains.

## Project

- [Contributing](https://selflearningplatform.github.io/docs/contributing.md): Contributions are welcome. Skills are edited in `agent/skills/`, never inside an agent's own folder.
